solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Text seen in margins of memoirs?

definitions.text: Text seen in margins of memoirs?

parts.words: Text seen in margins of memoirs?
parts.note: the first and last letters of the word memoirs are M and S, the standard abbreviation for a handwritten text

explanation.surface: A reader spots scribbled notes in the margins of someone's published memoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: The margins of 'memoirs' are its outer letters, M and S, and MS is the usual abbreviation for the answer, so the text is literally visible at the word's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten or typed original document, before printing, is what the abbreviation MS stands for.

clue.text: Inflict severe hurt on some in trauma immeasurably

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone inflicts great hurt on a few people already suffering immeasurable trauma.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple or mutilate someone is to wound them severely, a close synonym.

clue.text: Casino shifted around island capital

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
shifted says the letters of casino are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambling house has been relocated somewhere on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' turns CASINO into NICOSA, and 'around' puts I inside it, before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Fight with hard six-footer around posh saloon and totter?

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or brawl
a Merc is a Mercedes, an upmarket saloon car
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
an ant is an insect, which has six feet

explanation.surface: A brawl involving a tough tall man and a smart car, with someone staggering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' is not a tall person but an insect. A totter is old British slang for a rag-and-bone man, who collects and sells junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter, in British slang, is a rag-and-bone man who deals in scrap metal and junk.

clue.text: Priest out of sorts in middle of week getting early summons

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another
middle of picks the central letters of the word week

parts.note: feeling out of sorts means feeling ill

explanation.surface: A clergyman feeling unwell midweek gets called up early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the illness word between the two middle letters of 'week'; 'summons' is a noun here, a wake-up call.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning, a call to rise.

clue.text: Guide giving description of High Church congregation?

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious, a fair description of devout churchgoing
a lot is a group or gathering of people

explanation.surface: A guidebook describing the worshippers at a High Church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a 'pi lot', a pious bunch, the answer describes a devout congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or lead the way, and a pilot is one who steers.

clue.text: Go crazy if upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue sense means overturned, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An instruction to lose your mind if something goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb meaning leave, but it is the noun: have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt, the same as having a go.

clue.text: Namely, no ordinary expression curtailed messaging service

indicators.note: no says the following letter is dropped from the phrase for namely

parts.note: to wit is an old phrase meaning namely

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: Pedantic phrasing cut short on a social media platform.
explanation.walkthrough: TO WIT without O gives TWIT; TERM curtailed gives TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitter was the name of the short-post social media platform, an online messaging service.

clue.text: Piece in the US introducing novel and film — no lightweight publication?

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman, and piece is also slang for a woman
She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An American item featuring a book and a movie, in a weighty newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A broadsheet is a large-format, serious British newspaper, contrasted with the lighter tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-format papers are traditionally the serious quality press, the opposite of a lightweight tabloid.

clue.text: Run into old police and where they operated regressively

indicators.note: regressively means going backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the former police force
NI is Northern Ireland, where that force served

explanation.surface: Bumping into a former policeman back where he used to patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into debt or trouble is to bring it on yourself, which is to incur it.

clue.text: Old screen star in a lone TV hit

indicators.note: hit means struck and knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A former film star appears in a solitary television success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a noun for a success, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was a silent-film heartthrob of the 1920s, a star of the early screen.

clue.text: American fully dismantled basic social unit?

indicators.note: dismantled means taken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A US institution has been completely taken apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents and their children living together form the core household unit of society.

clue.text: Worldly old Greek character on board drawn to defend criminal act

indicators.note: on, with board, says letters go aboard, inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, and on board is the cue for going inside those letters
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: to defend means to guard by surrounding

parts.note: a drawn game is a tied one

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cultured ancient Greek on a ship is lured into defending a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Greek character' suggests one person but is two pieces. 'on board' means inside SS, a steamship; 'criminal' turns ACT into CAT, which 'to defend' puts inside the word for drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worldly is experienced and cultured, a close synonym.

clue.text: One exaggerating disorder in African country no good before onset of revolution

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: onset of picks the first letter of revolution

explanation.surface: A disturbance in an African state goes badly ahead of an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who feigns or exaggerates illness to dodge work is a classic shirker.

clue.text: Woman's horse with energy wholly returned

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

indicators.note: returned says the word for wholly comes back to front

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely

explanation.surface: A woman's horse comes back completely full of beans.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a woman's given name, so the clue gives an example.

clue.text: Comb given attention in school

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A hair comb gets noticed at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' looks like a noun but is the verb, to search thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to look through it carefully, a thorough hunt.

clue.text: Discontented son likes a furled garment

indicators.note: furled means rolled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order
discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters of son

explanation.surface: An unhappy son is fond of a rolled-up coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' empties son to its outer letters, which join 'likes a' as the pool that 'furled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat made from a seal's pelt is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Bug caught among favoured crowd

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the in-set is the fashionable clique
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A germ is picked up among a fashionable group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' could be an illness or a listening device; here it is a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is everyday speech for any small creepy-crawly such as a beetle.

clue.text: Uncomplaining masses in retrospective touring gallery

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reversed letters surround the next piece
retrospective means looking back, so the word for masses runs backwards

parts.note: lots means masses, a great many
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery

explanation.surface: Patient crowds attend a retrospective show at a touring gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' gives STOL; 'touring' wraps it round the London gallery's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures hardship patiently without grumbling.

clue.text: Formidable Arab getting special award flanked by retainer

indicators.note: flanked by means having something on each side, so the fee letters go round

parts.note: a retainer is a fee paid in advance for services
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
the OM is the Order of Merit, an honour

explanation.surface: An impressive Arab wins a special honour, with a servant at each side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' suggests a servant but is the fee paid in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formidable inspires fear or awe, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Herb found by tragic daughter in glasses

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: glasses are pictured as two rings, two letter Os
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A herb is discovered next to a tragic girl wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: OO for glasses is a crossword picture of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is wild marjoram, an aromatic plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Shot grabbed by lass before delay in awful media construct?

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl or lass
a lob is a high shot in tennis

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: vile means awful
lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A girl grabs a shot, then a delay in some awful media story.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshall McLuhan coined the phrase for the world shrunk by electronic media.
explanation.definitionFit: McLuhan's idea is that mass communication makes the whole world like one small community.

clue.text: Romanian lecturer staying in cut-off holiday hotel

indicators.note: staying in means remaining inside, so the letter goes within the shortened word
cut-off means docked, so the end of the word is chopped off

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Romanian academic stays at a remote holiday hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: VACATION cut to VAC takes L inside, giving VLAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vlachs are a Romance-speaking people of the Balkans, related to Romanians.

clue.text: Bird in wheeling motion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is recognised by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a turn is a wheeling or rotating movement

explanation.surface: A bird wheeling about in the sky makes itself heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a slender seabird related to gulls.

clue.text: People change course involving traditional school subject in competitive setting

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to tack is to change course when sailing
R stands for one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Students change course to study an old-fashioned subject competitively.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the traditional basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit for horses or cars is where contests of speed take place.

clue.text: Empty potty son left

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that letter is removed

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An empty chamber pot, the son having gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' suggests a child's chamber pot but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something empty of sense or meaning is silly and pointless.

clue.text: List press

definitions.meaning: a register or roster of names
to flatten something with a cylinder

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a register of names, and to roll is to flatten by pressing.

clue.text: Ramshackle area that's now developed around yard close to station

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the next piece
developed means changed and evolved, so the letters take a new order
close to means the end, picking the final letter of station

explanation.surface: A rundown district has been redeveloped round a railway yard near the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns THAT'S NOW into SHANTTOW, with Y inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of crude makeshift huts is a slum settlement.
